Step 23: Encrypt Feature State
↑ top

You can encrypt finalized Feature State at the persistence boundary with the AES-256-GCM Encrypt behavior. The pipeline continues to work with plain in-memory values; encryption runs after Resolve, Merge, Operators, Filters, and Reducers have completed and before the value is persisted.

Configure withAes256EncryptBehavior and call setAes256Secret() before initialization. The example uses a static salt so you can inspect and repeat the tutorial. In a secure application, create and retrieve salt material dynamically from an appropriate secure configuration source and keep it stable for data that must be decrypted later.

Take Action
  1. Open app.config.ts and register the AES-256 Encrypt behavior.
  2. Open example.service.ts and configure the tutorial secret and static salt before initialize().
  3. Use the Results panel to compare plain Feature State with the encrypted envelope.
What to Look For
  • Encryption does not change the value exposed by the FeatureCell.
  • AES-256-GCM provides confidentiality and integrity for persisted data.
  • The salt must be stable when previously persisted ciphertext must be restored.

Step 24: Persist Feature State
↑ top

Add withSessionStoragePersistBehavior after encryption to store the encrypted envelope in browser sessionStorage. Refresh the page and the persisted state remains available in that same tab. Close the tab and the session storage is cleared, so it is not durable application storage.

The example intentionally provides initialState while allowing persisted State to take priority. During hydration the persisted value is used by design; the initial value is not loaded into the active FeatureCell and is overwritten with undefined when no persisted value is available. This makes the persistence boundary explicit instead of silently mixing two sources of truth.

Take Action
  1. Register withSessionStoragePersistBehavior after the Encrypt behavior.
  2. Make a character change and inspect the persisted output.
  3. Refresh the page in the same tab and verify that the collection is restored.
What to Look For
  • Persist observes the finalized value after encryption and does not participate in state computation.
  • Session storage is scoped to one tab and survives reloads only within that tab.
  • Persisted State takes priority over initialState by design.

Step 25: Observe Pipeline Errors
↑ top

Extend the Filter stage with a simulated error and enable the global error service. When Throw Error is enabled, delete, add, and update candidates all fail in the filter before they can commit, encrypt, or persist. The current committed collection remains unchanged.

Observe the same failure in two independent ways. The global error service supports application-wide monitoring or a global error display and can be reset without changing Feature State. The fluent API's errors() callback receives the finalized error and snapshot for feature-specific observation.

Take Action
  1. Enable Throw Error.
  2. Try adding, editing, or deleting a character and observe the unchanged collection.
  3. Compare the global error display with the errors() emission output.
  4. Choose Reset Error to clear the global error and allow candidates through again.
What to Look For
  • The global error service is independent of the FeatureCell.
  • errors() observes finalized errors; it does not recover or transform the pipeline.
  • Resetting the global error is separate from resetting Feature State.

Step 26: Complete Encrypt and Persist Tutorial
↑ top

You now have a complete persistence boundary: pipeline stages compute and validate plain Feature State, AES-256 encrypts the finalized value, and session storage preserves it for reloads in the current tab. Errors stop the candidate before persistence while both global and feature-local observers can display what happened.

Take Action
  1. Refresh the page and confirm the session-scoped collection is restored.
  2. Close the tab, open the example again, and confirm that the tab-scoped value is gone.
  3. Trigger and reset the simulated error, then verify normal add, edit, and delete behavior.
Tutorial Summary
  • Encrypt and Persist behaviors run at the persistence boundary.
  • Static salt is acceptable only for this teaching example.
  • Global errors and errors() provide independent observation paths.
